## Original requirements (notes)

* Command line video editor for use by Claude for editing video
* Will be used to edit video footage from inside Claude
* We will provide footage.
* Some segments may be generated by Claude using tools such as Claude Motion.
* Use ffmpeg and associated tools
* Use rust for the tool itself
* Use case is to create youtube shorts, short and long videos
* Effects should be attractive to keep attention
* All the features that would be needed for professional looking and sounding videos
* Will use audio from https://elevenlabs.io/ (integrated as a plugin inside Claude).
* Not a general purpose editor. Created only for this purpose.
* Pull latest version of tools such as ffmpeg.
* We will not be selling this software. Only using it for internal purposes for editing. Edited videos will be published. Check licensing of all tools to confirm this is ok.
* Initially build for Mac but we intend to make available for Windows as well.

# Cutline: Implementation & Test Specification

**Working name:** `cutline` (binary and repo name; rename freely).
**Audience:** Claude Code, implementing autonomously across milestones.
**Status:** Spec v1, 2026-11-12.

## 0. Decisions captured from Q&A

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Interface | A declarative project file (JSON5 timeline). The CLI validates, previews, reviews and renders it. No imperative chain of edits. |
| ffmpeg | `cutline deps` auto-downloads the latest static ffmpeg/ffprobe builds. Version and SHA-256 are pinned in a lockfile. Each update is verified by selftest before it's promoted. |
| v1 scope | Animated captions, auto-reframe to 9:16, motion and text graphics, pro audio, plus the other features professional editing needs (jump cuts, color, transitions, B-roll, QA). |
| ElevenLabs | Claude supplies the files (VO, music, SFX, and optionally a Scribe transcript JSON). The editor makes **no** network or API calls to ElevenLabs. |
| Transcription | Local whisper.cpp with word timestamps. It can import an ElevenLabs Scribe word-timing JSON instead. |
| Generated assets | Opaque video (MP4/MOV), alpha overlays (ProRes 4444, WebM VP9 alpha, PNG sequences), and HTML/Lottie/SVG animations rendered via headless Chrome. |
| Self-test | Three parts: (1) `selftest` checks the toolchain and pipeline end to end on synthetic media; (2) automatic post-render QA; (3) a visual review pack for Claude. |
| Platforms | macOS (Apple Silicon first, Intel second), then Windows 10/11 x64. Code must be Windows-safe from day one. |

---

## 1. Instructions for Claude Code (read first)

1. **Work through milestones M0 to M9 in order without stopping for confirmation.** The user has pre-authorized all work in this spec inside the repo.
2. **Definition of done for every milestone.** Before moving on:
   - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
   - `cutline selftest --quick` passes. From M7 on, so does `--full` (it may skip, with a logged warning, any items that need unavailable OS features).
   - The milestone's acceptance tests (listed under that milestone) exist and pass.
   - `PROGRESS.md` is updated: milestone status, what was built, deviations from the spec and why, and known issues.
   - Git commit `M<n>: <summary>`. Tag `m<n>`.
3. **When blocked, don't stop.** Record the blocker in `PROGRESS.md › Blockers`, choose the most conservative workaround (mock, fallback, feature flag), and continue. Examples: a download fails, a model is unavailable, a platform feature is missing.
4. **Time-box.** If a sub-feature still fails after about 3 serious attempts, mark it `known_issue` in `PROGRESS.md`, put it behind a disabled flag if needed, and move on. Never weaken or delete a test to get a green build. Mark a test `#[ignore]` only with a reason string that names the known issue.
5. **Decisions log.** Record any non-trivial design choice not dictated here in `docs/decisions.md` (date, decision, alternatives, reason).
6. **Never** add network calls other than `cutline deps` downloads. Never call ElevenLabs or any other paid API. Never commit downloaded binaries or models. Commit only the lockfile.
7. Keep the **user-facing contract stable**: the project schema, CLI flags and JSON output shapes. Any breaking change needs a schema `version` bump and a migration note.
8. Prefer the boring, debuggable approach. Every render must be reproducible from `render --dry-run` output, which prints the exact ffmpeg commands and filter scripts.

---

## 2. Product overview

`cutline` is a single Rust CLI that Claude drives from a terminal. Claude:

1. Probes and analyzes the footage the user provides (`probe`, `analyze`, `transcribe`).
2. Writes a **project file** describing the edit.
3. Validates it (`validate`) and gets precise, machine-readable errors.
4. Looks at the edit (`review`): contact sheets, key frames, waveform and QA report, sized for Claude's vision input.
5. Iterates on the project file.
6. Renders final deliverables (`render`). Post-render QA runs automatically.

It is **not** a general-purpose NLE. Optimize for:

- YouTube Shorts (9:16, ≤ 3 min)
- short-form 16:9 (1–10 min)
- long-form 16:9 (10–60+ min)

It must produce professional, attention-holding results by default: punchy captions, motion, clean loud-enough audio, and no technical defects.

### Non-goals
GUI, real-time playback, multicam sync, HDR, 3D, collaborative editing, uploading to YouTube, generating media with AI (Claude does that with other tools).

---

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 Repo layout

```
cutline/
  Cargo.toml                # workspace
  crates/
    cutline-cli/            # clap CLI, JSON output, exit codes
    cutline-core/           # project model, JSON5 parse, schema, validation, time math, expansion of auto directives
    cutline-media/          # ffprobe wrapper, asset fingerprinting, proxies, cache
    cutline-render/         # timeline → render plan → ffmpeg commands/filter scripts; segment renderer; encoder profiles
    cutline-audio/          # mix graph, ducking envelopes, loudness (2-pass), voice chain presets
    cutline-text/           # ASS generation (captions, titles, lower thirds), font management, layout & safe zones
    cutline-transcribe/     # whisper.cpp integration, Scribe import, word timing, source→timeline word mapping
    cutline-reframe/        # face detection (ONNX), tracking, smoothing, crop path → sendcmd
    cutline-html/           # headless Chrome renderer for HTML/SVG/Lottie → alpha frames
    cutline-qa/             # post-render checks, review pack, selftest orchestration
    cutline-deps/           # downloads, lockfile, verification, tool discovery
    cutline-testkit/        # synthetic media generators, frame-ID encode/decode, tone analysis, golden image compare
  assets/
    fonts/                  # OFL fonts (see §12)
    luts/                   # a few permissively licensed .cube LUTs (or generated)
    templates/              # text/graphics templates (ASS-based and HTML-based)
    brand/default.json
    sfx/README.md           # SFX are user/ElevenLabs-supplied; folder convention only
  docs/
    CLAUDE_GUIDE.md         # how Claude should use the tool (also printed by `cutline guide`)
    PROJECT_FORMAT.md       # human docs for the schema
    decisions.md
  schema/project.schema.json  # generated from Rust types (schemars); checked in, test asserts up to date
  tests/                    # integration tests
  tools.lock.json           # pinned external tool versions + sha256
  PROGRESS.md
```

### 3.2 Key crates (permissive licenses only)
`clap`, `serde`, `serde_json`, `json5`, `schemars`, `thiserror`/`anyhow`, `tracing`, `rayon`, `tokio` (only where needed, e.g. the HTML renderer), `reqwest` (rustls) for deps, `sha2`, `zip`/`tar`/`xz2`/`flate2`, `image`, `insta` (snapshot tests), `whisper-rs` (whisper.cpp binding), `ort` (ONNX Runtime), `chromiumoxide` (CDP), `directories`, `tempfile`, `which`.
Enforce with `cargo-deny` (allow: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-DFS/3.0, MPL-2.0, Unlicense, CC0-1.0, BSL-1.0).

### 3.3 Processing model

```
project.json5
  → parse + schema validate + semantic validate
  → expand "auto" directives (jump cuts, filler removal, punch-in cadence, SFX on transitions) into explicit items
  → resolve timeline (absolute times, anchors, transitions overlap math)
  → render plan:
       video: list of SEGMENTS (each = one main clip incl. its effects/reframe, rendered to mezzanine)
              + transitions (xfade between adjacent segment mezzanines)
              + overlay pass (layers: b-roll, images, alpha video, HTML renders, ASS text/captions, progress bar)
       audio: stems (dialogue, vo, music, sfx) → processing chains → ducking → mix → 2-pass loudness → final WAV
  → final encode (video + audio mux) per target encoder profile
  → post-render QA → render_report.json (+ optional review pack)
```

- **Segment cache.** Segment mezzanines are content-addressed. The key is a hash of the asset fingerprint, the segment spec, the target geometry/fps, the cutline version and the ffmpeg version. Re-rendering after a caption tweak must not re-render segments.
- **Mezzanine format.** ProRes 422 HQ (`prores_ks`, yuv422p10le) for opaque video and ProRes 4444 (`yuva444p10le`) for alpha. Audio is PCM float 48 kHz.
- **Filter scripts.** Always write filtergraphs to files and pass them by file. Use `-/filter_complex <file>` on ffmpeg ≥ 7.1, otherwise `-filter_complex_script`; detect the version. This avoids the Windows command-line length limit.
- **No shell.** Spawn processes with `std::process::Command` and explicit args. Never build shell strings.
- **Parallelism.** Render segments in parallel (default `num_cpus/2` concurrent ffmpeg jobs, configurable).

### 3.4 Time model
- Internally, store all times as **rational** values (frames at the timeline fps, plus sample-accurate audio). Accept seconds (`12.4`), timecode strings (`"01:02.500"`, `"00:01:02.500"`) and frames (`"f:372"`).
- Snap video cuts to the nearest output frame. Audio cuts use 10 ms micro-fades by default to avoid clicks.
- **Main storyline:** an ordered list of clips. A transition of duration `d` between A and B overlaps the tail of A and the head of B, so the timeline shrinks by `d`. Validation fails if `d` exceeds either neighbor's duration minus 1 frame.
- **Layers:** placed at absolute timeline time (`start`, `end` | `duration`), or **anchored** to a main clip id (`{"anchor": "clip_id", "offset": 0.5}`), so they follow ripple edits.
- `"end"` keyword = timeline end.

## 4. Project file format (v1)

JSON5 (comments and trailing commas allowed); plain JSON is also accepted. `cutline schema` prints the JSON Schema. `docs/PROJECT_FORMAT.md` documents every field with defaults.

```json5
{
  version: 1,
  name: "knife-sharpening-short",
  target: "shorts",              // shorts | long_1080p | long_4k | square | custom (see §8)
  fps: 30,                       // default from target
  brand: "brand/default.json",   // fonts, colors, logo, caption style defaults, SFX names
  assets: {
    take1:  { path: "footage/take1.mov" },
    vo:     { path: "audio/vo.mp3", role: "voice", transcript: "audio/vo.scribe.json" },
    music:  { path: "audio/music.mp3", role: "music" },
    intro:  { path: "gen/intro.html", kind: "html", duration: 2.5, alpha: true, params: { title: "Sharp in 60s" } },
    callout:{ path: "gen/arrow.mov" },            // ProRes 4444 with alpha, auto-detected
    logo:   { path: "brand/logo.png" },
    whoosh: { path: "sfx/whoosh.wav", role: "sfx" },
  },
  main: [
    { id: "hook", clip: "take1", in: "00:12.40", out: "00:18.90",
      reframe: { mode: "track_face" },                 // track_face | center | manual | fit_blur | split
      color: { lut: "warm_film", intensity: 0.6, exposure: 0.1 },
      effects: [ { type: "punch_in", at: 2.0, scale: 1.18, duration: 0.25, ease: "out_cubic" } ] },
    { transition: { type: "whip_left", duration: 0.25, sfx: "whoosh" } },
    { id: "step1", clip: "take1", in: "01:02.00", out: "01:09.50", speed: 1.1 },
    { transition: { type: "zoom_in", duration: 0.3 } },
    { id: "outro", clip: "take1", in: "02:10.00", out: "02:14.00", audio: "duck" },
  ],
  layers: [
    { type: "html",  asset: "intro", start: 0, z: 10 },
    { type: "text",  template: "hook_title", start: 0, duration: 2.2, text: "Your knife is dull because of THIS" },
    { type: "video", asset: "callout", anchor: "step1", offset: 1.0, position: { x: 0.62, y: 0.40 }, scale: 0.5 },
    { type: "broll", asset: "take1", src_in: "03:00", src_out: "03:03", anchor: "step1", offset: 2.0, fit: "cover", audio: false },
    { type: "image", asset: "logo", start: 0, end: "end", position: "top_right", scale: 0.12, opacity: 0.85 },
    { type: "progress_bar", style: "brand" },
    { type: "audio", asset: "music", start: 0, end: "end", gain_db: -4, fade_in: 0.5, fade_out: 1.5 },
    { type: "sfx", asset: "whoosh", at: 5.2, gain_db: -3 },
  ],
  captions: {
    source: "auto",              // auto (transcribe/import, mapped through the edit) | file | none
    style: "bold_pop",           // see §6.5
    position: "lower_mid",
    max_words_per_line: 3,
    corrections: { "chefs knife": "chef's knife" },
    emphasis: ["THIS", "sharp"], // words styled with accent color / scale
  },
  audio: {
    loudness: { integrated: -14, true_peak: -1.0 },
    voice_chain: "clean_voice",  // see §6.4
    duck: { under: ["voice"], target: ["music"], amount_db: -12, attack: 0.12, release: 0.45 },
  },
  auto: {
    jump_cuts: { enabled: true, min_silence: 0.35, keep_padding: 0.08, applies_to: ["take1"] },
    remove_fillers: { enabled: true, words: ["um", "uh", "erm"] },
    punch_ins: { every: 4.0, scale: [1.08, 1.15], skip_if_other_motion: true },
    sfx_on_transitions: "whoosh",
  },
  exports: [ { target: "shorts" } ],           // multiple targets allowed (e.g., shorts + long_1080p from one edit)
}
```

**Rules**
- Asset paths resolve relative to the project file. `kind` is auto-detected from ffprobe and extension (`video`, `image`, `audio`, `image_sequence` via a printf pattern `frames/%05d.png`, or `html`/`lottie`/`svg`).
- WebM VP9 alpha **must be decoded with `-c:v libvpx-vp9`**, because the native vp9 decoder drops alpha. Detect `alpha_mode=1` in the stream tags.
- `cutline expand project.json5` prints the fully explicit timeline after auto directives are applied, so Claude can see and freeze it.
- Validation errors are JSON: `{code, path (JSON pointer), message, hint}`. Examples: `E_TIME_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `E_UNKNOWN_ASSET`, `E_TRANSITION_TOO_LONG`, `E_FONT_MISSING`, `E_ALPHA_NOT_PRESENT`, `W_CAPTION_OUTSIDE_SAFE_ZONE`, `W_SHORTS_OVER_LIMIT`.

**Brand file** (`brand/default.json`): fonts (title, body, caption), colors (primary, accent, text, stroke, background), logo asset, default caption style, lower-third template, intro/outro assets, SFX aliases (`whoosh`, `pop`, `ding`, `riser`), LUT default, and watermark position.

## 5. CLI

Every command supports `--json` (machine output on stdout, logs on stderr) and returns meaningful exit codes: 0 ok, 1 validation/QA error, 2 usage error, 3 tool/dependency error, 4 internal error.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `cutline doctor` | Check tools and versions, required ffmpeg filters/encoders/decoders, fonts, models, Chrome and disk space. Prints a fix-it list. |
| `cutline deps install [--all\|ffmpeg\|whisper-model <name>\|face-model\|chrome]` | Download into the tools dir (§9). |
| `cutline deps update [--check]` | Fetch the latest upstream versions, verify them with `selftest --quick` against the new tools, then promote. Keeps the previous version for `deps rollback`. |
| `cutline deps status` | Show installed versions against the lockfile. |
| `cutline probe <file>...` | Normalized JSON media info: duration, streams, fps (incl. VFR detection), rotation, color, alpha, loudness (fast). |
| `cutline analyze <file>` | Scene cuts (`scdet`), silences, loudness curve, face presence summary, black/freeze spans. Cached. |
| `cutline transcribe <file> [--model] [--lang] [--import-scribe f.json]` | Word-level transcript JSON (§6.5). Cached. |
| `cutline init [--target shorts] [--assets dir]` | Scaffold a project, brand file and folders. |
| `cutline schema` / `cutline guide` | Print the JSON Schema / print CLAUDE_GUIDE.md. |
| `cutline templates list [--json]` | Text/graphics/caption templates and transitions, with parameters. |
| `cutline validate <project>` | Schema and semantic validation. |
| `cutline expand <project>` | Explicit timeline after auto directives, as JSON5, plus a human-readable EDL table. |
| `cutline preview <project> --at <t>... \| --range a-b [--safe-zones]` | Still PNGs or a 540p proxy clip. Fast path: proxies plus the veryfast encoder. |
| `cutline review <project> [--out review/]` | Review pack (§7.3). Uses a draft render if no final exists. |
| `cutline render <project> [--export name] [--draft] [--dry-run] [--no-cache] [--allow-qa-errors]` | Final render, then QA. |
| `cutline qa <video> --target shorts [--project p]` | Run QA on any file. |
| `cutline thumbnail <project> --at <t> --text "..." [--template]` | 1280×720 (or 1080×1920) JPG/PNG. |
| `cutline chapters <project>` | YouTube chapter list from main clip ids or markers (`00:00 Intro`…). |
| `cutline selftest [--quick\|--full] [--keep]` | §7.1 |
| `cutline cache stats\|clean` | Manage cache. |

## 6. Features (functional spec)

### 6.1 Editing core
- Trim, concatenate, and ripple via anchors. Speed change (0.25×–4×) uses `setpts` for video and chained `atempo` for audio, so pitch is preserved. Speed ramps take a keyframed speed curve.
- Freeze frame (`{type:"freeze", at, duration}`), reverse (short clips only), and mute/duck/replace for clip audio.
- Source normalization: VFR goes to CFR at the timeline fps; rotation metadata is honored; SAR is fixed; color is converted to BT.709 (via `zscale` if available, else `colorspace`/`scale` with flags).
- Geometry modes per clip when the source aspect ≠ the target: `cover` (crop), `fit_blur` (fit with a blurred, scaled background fill), `fit_pad` (brand color), `track_face` (§6.6), `manual` (keyframed crop rectangle), and `split` (two regions stacked vertically for 9:16, e.g. two speakers or screen + face).
- Stabilization (optional, if the ffmpeg build has `vidstab`): `stabilize: {strength}`. Two-pass, cached.

### 6.2 Motion & transitions (attention features)
- **Punch-in / zoom:** smooth scale and position animation with easing (`linear`, `in/out/in_out` × `quad/cubic/expo`, `back`, `spring`). There must be no sub-pixel jitter. Implement by upscaling to 2× working resolution, then cropping with expression-driven `crop` (or an equivalent smooth method). `zoompan` alone is not acceptable unless the smoothness test passes.
- **Ken Burns** on stills and B-roll.
- **Shake** (impact), **flash** (white or brand-color frame flash), **blur-in**, **RGB-split glitch** (via `rgbashift`), **vignette**, and **motion blur** on whips (via `tmix`/`minterpolate`, short durations only).
- **Transitions:** all relevant ffmpeg `xfade` types (fade, fadeblack, fadewhite, wipeleft/right/up/down, slideleft/right/up/down, smoothleft/right, circleopen/close, radial, zoomin, pixelize, hblur, dissolve…), plus custom composites: `whip_left/right/up/down` (fast slide + directional blur + optional SFX), `zoom_punch`, `flash_cut`, `glitch`. Audio uses a matching `acrossfade` (curve configurable) or a hard cut with micro-fades.
- **Overlays:** B-roll (full or PiP with rounded corners, border and shadow), images, alpha video, image sequences, HTML renders. Each overlay takes position/anchor presets, scale, rotation, opacity, z-order, and enter/exit animations (`fade`, `slide_*`, `pop`, `scale_in`).
- **Progress bar** (Shorts retention): thin bar at top or bottom in the brand accent color, length proportional to timeline progress.
- **Color:** `.cube` LUT via `lut3d` with an intensity blend, exposure, contrast, saturation, temperature/tint (via `colortemperature`/`colorbalance`), and sharpen (`unsharp`). Presets: `natural`, `punchy`, `warm_film`, `cool_clean`, `bw_contrast`.

### 6.3 Text & graphics
- Text rendering goes through **libass** (`subtitles` filter on generated `.ass` files) with `fontsdir` pointing to bundled fonts, so Mac and Windows render identically. Don't rely on system fonts.
- **Templates** (ASS-based in M4, with HTML-based alternatives in M8):
  - `hook_title`: big centered title with pop-in, stroke and shadow.
  - `lower_third`: name and subtitle with a bar that slides in.
  - `callout`: arrow/box plus label.
  - `step_counter`: "Step 2/5".
  - `big_number`, `quote`, `cta_subscribe`, `end_card`.
  - `emoji_pop`: Noto Emoji PNGs, bundled, with a scale pop.
- Template parameters: text, colors (default to brand), font, size, position, animation in/out, duration, and emphasis words.
- **Safe zones:** each target defines a safe rectangle. For Shorts the default avoids the top 10%, the bottom 22% (title/description UI) and the right 16% (action buttons); it's configurable. The layout engine auto-wraps and auto-shrinks text to fit. `preview --safe-zones` draws the zones.
- Escaping: correct ASS escaping (`{}`, `\N`, commas) and ffmpeg filter escaping, **including Windows drive-letter paths** in the `subtitles=` filter (`C\:/...`). Unit-test both.

### 6.4 Audio (pro sound)
- **Roles:** `dialogue` (main clip audio), `voice` (VO), `music`, `sfx`. Each role has its own processing chain, then they're mixed.
- **Voice chain presets:**
  - `clean_voice`: highpass 80 Hz → `afftdn` denoise (moderate) → de-ess (`deesser`) → presence EQ (+2 dB @ 3–5 kHz, −2 dB @ 250–400 Hz) → `acompressor` (≈3:1) → limiter.
  - `podcast_warm`
  - `raw` (no processing)
  - `arnndn` neural denoise is an optional preset, only when its model's license has been verified.
- **Ducking:** compute speech activity from the transcript word timings, falling back to an energy-based VAD. Build a smooth gain envelope with attack/release and apply it to the target roles via `volume` with keyframes (sendcmd/`volume=eval=frame`). This is deterministic and easy to visualize. `sidechaincompress` is an alternative mode.
- **Fades** on every clip boundary (micro-fades by default), plus music fades in and out.
- **SFX:** placed at times or auto-placed on transitions/punch-ins (`auto.sfx_on_transitions`). Each one has gain and an optional random pick from a set.
- **Loudness:** two-pass `loudnorm` (measure, then apply with linear mode where possible) on the final mix. Defaults: −14 LUFS integrated, −1.0 dBTP true peak, LRA ≤ 11 (long form) / ≤ 7 (shorts). Configurable per target.
- Output: 48 kHz, stereo, AAC-LC 320 kb/s (native `aac` encoder; `libfdk_aac` isn't in the builds and is non-free).

### 6.5 Transcription & captions
- **Engine:** whisper.cpp via `whisper-rs`, with Metal on macOS and CPU/CUDA on Windows. Default model is `large-v3-turbo` quantized (q5_0); `--fast` uses `base.en`. Enable word-level timestamps (token timestamps, plus DTW alignment where supported). If `whisper-rs` fails to build on a platform, fall back to a sidecar `whisper-cli` binary.
- **Import:** an ElevenLabs Scribe JSON with word timings is converted to the internal transcript format. Prefer it for VO assets when it's supplied.
- **Transcript format:** `{asset, lang, model, words:[{w, start, end, conf, speaker?}], segments:[...]}`. Cached by asset fingerprint and model.
- **Mapping:** transcripts belong to source assets. Words are mapped through the edit (in/out, speed, jump cuts) into timeline time; words that were cut out are dropped. This is how captions survive re-edits without re-transcribing.
- **Corrections:** apply the `corrections` map and the brand dictionary (names, product terms) after transcription.
- **Caption styles** (all ASS-generated):
  - `bold_pop`: 1–3 words at a time, centered, heavy font, thick stroke. The current word gets the accent color and a 105–115% scale pop.
  - `karaoke`: full line with a progressive word highlight.
  - `word_by_word`: one word at a time, with a punch scale.
  - `clean_sentence`: 1–2 line sentence captions for long form, with a soft box.
  - `boxed`: words on a rounded colored box.
  - `emphasis` words get the accent color and optional emoji.
- **Rules:** max chars/line (default 22 for Shorts, 42 for long form); reading speed warning above 20 cps; no caption crossing a hard cut by less than 2 frames; never outside the safe zone.
- **Edit assist (auto directives):**
  - `jump_cuts`: remove silences longer than `min_silence`, keeping `keep_padding`. Uses transcript gaps plus `silencedetect`, intersected.
  - `remove_fillers`: cut filler words using word timings, with micro-fades.
  - `punch_ins`: insert alternating punch-ins every N seconds where no other motion exists (a pattern interrupt).
  - All of these expand to explicit, inspectable timeline items (`cutline expand`).

### 6.6 Auto-reframe (16:9 → 9:16 and others)
- **Detector:** YuNet face detection ONNX model via `ort` (ONNX Runtime), running on frames decoded by ffmpeg at a reduced analysis rate (default 6 fps, 640px wide) through a raw video pipe. Cached per asset and range.
- **Subject selection:** `largest`, `most_persistent` (default), `left`/`right`, or `index`. Optional `speaker` mode biases toward the face whose region best correlates with transcript speech activity. This mode is best-effort; mark it experimental.
- **Path smoothing:** dead-zone (don't move for small offsets), critically damped spring or One-Euro filter, max pan speed, ease into new subjects. Reset at scene cuts (`scdet`). Hold the last position when detection is lost; drift to center after a timeout.
- **Output:** a per-frame crop rectangle, written as an ffmpeg `sendcmd` file driving `crop` x/y (or as expressions), then scaled to the target.
- **Overrides:** `reframe: {mode:"manual", keys:[{t, x, y, zoom}]}` and `reframe.bias` (e.g. keep the subject at x=0.5, y=0.38 for headroom).
- **Fallbacks:** `fit_blur` when no faces are found in a clip (configurable). Warn in validate/review output.
- Layout `split`: auto-detect two faces → stacked layout; or explicit rectangles.

### 6.7 HTML / SVG / Lottie renderer (generated motion graphics)
- **Chrome:** headless Chrome via `chromiumoxide` (CDP). Use the installed Chrome or Edge, or `deps install chrome` (Chrome for Testing headless shell).
- **Deterministic time:** for each frame `t`:
  - Pause all `document.getAnimations()` and set `currentTime = t*1000`.
  - Call the page's optional `window.__cutline_seek(t)` hook.
  - For Lottie, use bundled `lottie-web` with `goToAndStop(frame, true)`.
  - For SVG, use SMIL `setCurrentTime(t)`.
  - Wait for fonts and images to load before the first frame.
- **Viewport & alpha:** viewport = target or layer size, with device scale factor for crispness. Transparent background (`Emulation.setDefaultBackgroundColorOverride` with alpha 0) when `alpha: true`. Capture PNG frames, then encode to ProRes 4444 mezzanine. Cache by HTML content hash, params and size.
- **Params:** `params` are injected as `window.__cutline_params` before load, so one template serves many videos.
- **Sandbox:** network disabled by default (only local file access under the project dir); 30 s per-frame timeout.

### 6.8 Thumbnails & chapters
- `thumbnail`: frame grab (optionally with face-aware crop) + template text + brand. Outputs 1280×720 for long form, 1080×1920 for Shorts.
- `chapters`: from clip ids/markers. The first chapter must be 00:00, with ≥ 3 chapters, each ≥ 10 s (YouTube rules). Warn otherwise.

---

## 7. Self-test, QA and review (the "self-test mode")

### 7.1 `cutline selftest`
Synthetic media comes from `cutline-testkit` and is generated with ffmpeg `lavfi`. The selftest needs no user footage.

**Frame-ID video**
- Each source frame encodes its frame index as a 16-bit binary block pattern: 16 blocks of 64×64, pure black or white, in the top row.
- Each source also has a distinct background color and gradient, plus a `testsrc2` region for visual sanity.
- `decode_frame_id(png) -> u16` reads the block means. It must survive the x264 encode at CRF 18 and the scaling to 1080×1920 (test this).

**Tone audio:** each source carries a distinct sine frequency (e.g. 440, 660, 880 Hz). Beep+flash pairs are used for A/V sync tests.

**Speech:** macOS `say -o`, or Windows SAPI via PowerShell, synthesizes a known sentence for the whisper tests. If neither is available, skip with a warning.

**Alpha overlays:** ProRes 4444 and VP9 alpha test overlays (a moving circle with known alpha), plus a PNG sequence.

**HTML/Lottie:** a tiny HTML page with a CSS animation that moves a box linearly, and a Lottie JSON doing the same. Assert box position vs. t.

**Face fixture:** `tests/fixtures/face_*.jpg`, from a CC0 / public-domain source documented in `tests/fixtures/SOURCES.md`, panned across a 16:9 canvas via ffmpeg. If the fixture isn't available, run reframe tests against an injected mock detector and mark the real-model test skipped.

**`--quick`** (target < 90 s on an M-series Mac):
1. Doctor checks pass (tools, filters, encoders, fonts).
2. Render a 6 s Shorts project: 3 clips, 1 xfade, 1 whip, punch-in, text template, captions from a fixture transcript, music duck, logo, progress bar.
3. Assert exact frame mapping: decode frame IDs at sampled timeline frames and compare with the expected source frames from the plan.
4. Assert tone frequencies per segment via FFT at sampled times.
5. Run QA (§7.2); there must be no errors.

**`--full`** adds:
- every transition type
- every caption style (golden images)
- every text template (golden images)
- whisper on synthesized speech (WER ≤ 15% on the fixed sentence; word timing within ±150 ms of the `say` alignment where available, else monotonicity and coverage checks)
- reframe tracking error: the crop center stays within 8% of frame width of the true face center after settling, and pan speed stays under the configured max
- HTML/Lottie position accuracy within ±2 px
- alpha correctness (pixel samples)
- loudness accuracy (±0.5 LU on synthetic material)
- A/V sync (|offset| ≤ 1 frame)
- a punch-in smoothness test: the per-frame scale/position delta must be monotone and jitter-free, with no reversals during ease-out; measure via a high-contrast grid fixture and phase correlation
- a performance benchmark recorded to `selftest_report.json`

**Output:** `selftest_report.json` (per check: id, status pass/fail/skip, measured, threshold, duration, artifact paths) and a short human summary. Exit code 1 on any fail.

### 7.2 Post-render QA (runs automatically after every `render`)
Checks with severities:

| Check | Default rule | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| Container/codec | MP4, H.264 High, yuv420p, AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo, `+faststart` | error |
| Geometry/fps | Matches target exactly; CFR | error |
| Color tags | BT.709 primaries/transfer/matrix, tv range | error |
| Duration | Timeline duration ±1 frame; Shorts ≤ 180 s | error |
| A/V alignment | Stream start = 0, durations within 1 frame | error |
| Loudness | Integrated within ±1 LU of target; true peak ≤ target; report LRA | error (LU), warn (LRA) |
| Clipping | Sample peaks ≥ −0.1 dBFS count = 0 | warn |
| Silence | No digital silence > 1.5 s unless marked intentional | warn |
| Black frames | `blackdetect` > 0.3 s unless intended (e.g. fade) | warn |
| Freeze | `freezedetect` > 1.0 s unless a freeze effect is used | warn |
| First frame | Not black/blank (hook) | warn |
| Hook (shorts) | Caption or text visible within the first 1.0 s | warn |
| Captions | All caption boxes inside the safe zone (computed from layout); cps ≤ 20 | warn |
| Bitrate | Within the target profile range | info |

Output: `<out>.qa.json`. `render` exits 1 if there's any error, unless `--allow-qa-errors`.

### 7.3 Review pack (`cutline review`)
Everything Claude needs to *see* the edit, sized for vision input (longest side ≤ 1568 px; at most ~20 images):
- `contact_sheet.jpg`: a grid of frames every N s (auto-chosen so there are ≤ 24 tiles), each stamped with timecode and clip id.
- `cuts/*.jpg`: the frames just before and after each cut/transition midpoint (side by side).
- `captions/*.jpg`: samples of caption frames with safe-zone overlay.
- `reframe/*.jpg`: the source frame with the crop rectangle drawn, at several times per tracked clip.
- `audio.png`: the waveform per role (voice, music, sfx), the final mix, the duck envelope, and the momentary loudness curve with the target line.
- `timeline.txt`: a human-readable EDL with timeline-in/out, source-in/out, effects, layers and captions text.
- `qa.json` and `summary.md`: QA results and a list of "suggested improvements". For example: no visual change for > 5 s, caption reading speed too high, music too loud relative to voice (> −18 LU difference flagged), hook missing.
- `preview_540p.mp4`: a fast draft render.

---

## 8. Targets & encoder profiles

| Target | Geometry | fps | Video encode (final) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shorts` | 1080×1920 | 30 (or 60) | libx264 `-preset slow -crf 18 -profile:v high -level 4.2 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g fps/2 -bf 2 -movflags +faststart` | ≤ 180 s, safe zones on |
| `long_1080p` | 1920×1080 | 24/25/30/60 (follow source) | same | chapters, end-screen safe area in the last 20 s |
| `long_4k` | 3840×2160 | follow source | libx264 crf 18 (HEVC optional later) | slower; segment cache important |
| `square` | 1080×1080 | 30 | same | |
| `custom` | any | any | configurable | |

- `--draft` uses `h264_videotoolbox` on Mac and `h264_nvenc`/`h264_qsv`/`h264_amf` on Windows when available, at 540p or 720p. Final renders always use libx264 unless `--hw` is set.
- Set color tags explicitly: `-color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709 -color_range tv`.

---

## 9. External tools & `cutline deps`

**Tools dir:** macOS `~/Library/Application Support/cutline/tools`; Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cutline\tools`. The cache lives under the platform cache dir. Override both with `CUTLINE_HOME`.

| Tool | Source (default) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ffmpeg/ffprobe (macOS arm64) | Martin Riedl static builds (`ffmpeg.martin-riedl.de`), release channel | GPL build including x264, libass, freetype, vidstab, libvpx |
| ffmpeg/ffprobe (macOS x86_64) | evermeet.cx | GPL static |
| ffmpeg/ffprobe (Windows x64) | BtbN GitHub releases, `ffmpeg-master-latest-win64-gpl` or the latest `n7.x` gpl | Prefer the latest *release* branch over master for stability |
| Fallback | System ffmpeg (Homebrew/winget) if it passes `doctor` capability checks | |
| whisper models | Hugging Face `ggerganov/whisper.cpp` ggml files | SHA-256 recorded |
| YuNet ONNX | OpenCV Zoo `face_detection_yunet` | |
| ONNX Runtime | via the `ort` crate download-binaries, or a pinned release | |
| Chrome headless shell | Chrome for Testing JSON endpoints | Or use the installed Chrome/Edge |
| lottie-web | npm tarball (pinned) | Vendored into assets at build time, or downloaded |

- **Lockfile** `tools.lock.json`: for each tool, record name, version, platform, URL, sha256, install date and selftest result.
- `deps update` resolves the latest versions, downloads them to a staging dir, runs `selftest --quick` with the staged tools, and promotes them only on pass. Otherwise it keeps the current tools and reports why.
- `doctor` verifies these capabilities. **Filters:** `xfade`, `acrossfade`, `loudnorm`, `ebur128`, `afftdn`, `deesser`, `acompressor`, `sidechaincompress`, `subtitles` (libass), `lut3d`, `scdet`, `blackdetect`, `freezedetect`, `silencedetect`, `rgbashift`, `colortemperature`, plus optional `zscale` and `vidstab*`. **Encoders:** `libx264`, `aac`, `prores_ks`, `png`. **Decoders:** `libvpx-vp9`, `prores`, `hevc`, `h264`. Missing required capabilities are errors; missing optional ones degrade features with warnings.

---

## 10. Milestones (implement in order)

Each milestone lists its scope and its **acceptance tests**. Those tests are required in `cargo test` or in the selftest.

### M0: Foundation
Scope:
- Workspace scaffold, CI config (GitHub Actions: macOS-14 arm64 + windows-latest; Windows may be allowed to fail until M9), `cargo-deny`, the `tracing` setup, and JSON output conventions with exit codes.
- `cutline-deps`: downloads, extraction, sha256, the lockfile, and tool discovery (tools dir → PATH fallback).
- The `doctor`, `deps install ffmpeg`, `deps status` and `probe` commands.
- `cutline-testkit`: the synthetic media generators and frame-ID encode/decode.

Acceptance:
- `deps install ffmpeg` on macOS installs a working ffmpeg and records it in the lockfile.
- `doctor --json` lists the capabilities.
- `probe` on testkit media returns the correct duration, fps, resolution and alpha flag for the ProRes 4444 and VP9-alpha fixtures.
- Frame-ID round-trip survives an x264 CRF 23 encode and a scale to 1080×1920 (100% decode accuracy over 300 frames).

### M1: Project model & basic render
Scope:
- Rust types plus JSON5 parsing, `schemars` schema generation (a checked-in schema plus a test that it's current), semantic validation with JSON-pointer errors, and the time model (§3.4).
- `validate`, `schema`, `init` and `expand` (no auto directives yet).
- Render plan for the main storyline: trims, concat, geometry modes `cover`/`fit_pad`/`fit_blur`, and normalization (VFR→CFR, rotation, color).
- Segment mezzanines with the cache, a final libx264/AAC encode, `render --dry-run` and `preview --at`.

Acceptance:
- Golden snapshot tests (`insta`) for the filter scripts generated from fixture projects.
- An invalid-project test suite: ≥ 20 cases, each asserting its error code and JSON path.
- Exact frame-mapping test on a 5-clip render: every sampled frame's decoded ID equals the expected source frame.
- Changing only one clip re-renders only that segment (cache hit count asserted).
- Windows path escaping unit tests.

### M2: Audio pipeline
Scope:
- Roles and stems, per-role chains (voice presets), music/VO/SFX layers, fades and micro-fades.
- Transcript-or-VAD speech activity, then the ducking envelope.
- Two-pass loudness, the audio part of QA, and the `audio.png` renderer.

Acceptance:
- Loudness of the final mix is within ±0.5 LU of target on synthetic material; true peak ≤ −1.0 dBTP.
- Ducking: music RMS during speech regions is lower by `amount_db` ±1.5 dB, and attack/release timing is within ±50 ms.
- No clicks at cuts: no sample-to-sample discontinuity above threshold at cut points.
- Tone-per-segment FFT test passes with transitions present.

### M3: Motion, transitions, overlays, color
Scope:
- Every xfade transition plus custom whips/zoom-punch/flash/glitch, with audio crossfades.
- Punch-in/zoom/Ken Burns with easing; shake, flash, blur and vignette.
- Speed and speed ramps, freeze.
- Overlays (image, alpha video, image sequence, B-roll/PiP with rounded corners/shadow) with enter/exit animations and the progress bar.
- LUT and color controls, and anchoring of layers to clip ids.

Acceptance:
- Timeline duration with transitions equals the expected value to the frame.
- Smoothness test for punch-in (§7.1).
- Alpha overlay pixel tests: the composited color matches the expected alpha blend within ±3/255.
- Anchored layers move correctly when an earlier clip is lengthened.
- A golden image test for each transition at its midpoint (SSIM ≥ 0.97 vs. the blessed image; bless with `CUTLINE_BLESS=1`).

### M4: Text & graphics
Scope:
- ASS generation engine, bundled fonts with `fontsdir`, and the template system.
- `hook_title`, `lower_third`, `callout`, `step_counter`, `big_number`, `quote`, `cta_subscribe`, `end_card`, `emoji_pop`.
- The brand file, safe zones with auto-fit, `preview --safe-zones`, and `templates list`.

Acceptance:
- Golden images per template on both Shorts and 16:9.
- Auto-fit keeps a long title inside the safe zone (bounding box computed via a libass-equivalent measurement, or by rendering text on a transparent frame and measuring its alpha bbox).
- ASS escaping unit tests.
- Identical renders whether system fonts are present or not (the test runs with an empty system font fallback).

### M5: Transcription, captions, edit assist
Scope:
- whisper-rs integration with a model download, Scribe JSON import, the transcript cache, and the corrections map.
- Source→timeline word mapping and all caption styles.
- The `jump_cuts`, `remove_fillers`, `punch_ins` and `sfx_on_transitions` auto directives, and `expand` showing the results.

Acceptance:
- Word-mapping unit tests: speed changes, jump cuts and transitions all map correctly, and dropped words are excluded.
- WER and timing tests on synthesized speech (macOS).
- Golden images for each caption style.
- Jump-cut test: a synthetic file with known silence gaps produces cuts at the expected points (±1 frame), and the output contains no silences longer than `min_silence`.
- Filler-removal test on fixture transcripts.
- Scribe import test using a hand-made fixture JSON in the documented Scribe shape. Keep the parser tolerant of extra fields.

### M6: Auto-reframe
Scope:
- The YuNet+ort detector with the analysis cache, subject selection, smoothing, scene-cut resets and the sendcmd crop path.
- Manual keys, the `fit_blur` fallback, the `split` layout, and reframe images in the review pack.

Acceptance:
- On the panned face fixture, tracking error stays ≤ 8% of width after the settle time, there's no jitter (crop x delta sign changes ≤ 2 per second when the subject moves monotonically), and pan speed stays ≤ max.
- With a mock detector: unit tests for dead-zone, hold, drift-to-center and scene-cut reset.
- Fallback to `fit_blur` when no faces are found, with a warning emitted.

### M7: QA, review pack, selftest complete
Scope:
- All §7.2 checks, the full §7.3 review pack, and `selftest --full` with the report.
- `qa` as a standalone command, suggested improvements, and the `render` gating.

Acceptance:
- Fault-injection tests: deliberately broken outputs (wrong fps, loud audio, a 2 s black gap, missing faststart, captions outside the safe zone) each trigger the expected QA finding.
- Review-pack images meet the size limits and image count budget.
- `selftest --full` passes on macOS.

### M8: HTML / SVG / Lottie
Scope:
- `cutline-html` (§6.7), `deps install chrome`, the vendored lottie-web, the alpha mezzanine and the cache.
- HTML variants of the `hook_title`, `lower_third` and `end_card` templates, plus params injection.

Acceptance:
- Position accuracy tests for CSS, Lottie and SVG (±2 px at sampled frames).
- Alpha preserved.
- Deterministic output: two renders of the same template are byte-identical PNG frames.
- A network-access attempt from the page is blocked.

### M9: Windows, packaging, docs, polish
Scope:
- Windows CI green, Windows ffmpeg/Chrome/model download paths, and hardware draft encoders.
- `thumbnail`, `chapters`, multi-export from one project, and the `cache` commands.
- `docs/CLAUDE_GUIDE.md` (the workflow Claude should follow, see §11), `docs/PROJECT_FORMAT.md` and a README.
- A release build script for a universal macOS binary and Windows zip, plus the `deps update` flow end to end.

Acceptance:
- The full test suite and `selftest --quick` pass on windows-latest CI (whisper and reframe may use CPU).
- Paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters work on both OSes (fixture with `ü` and spaces in folder names).
- `deps update` on a simulated new version stages, selftests, promotes and rolls back correctly. Test with a local mock HTTP server.

## 11. CLAUDE_GUIDE.md (content outline; ship with the tool)

**Default workflow for Claude when editing:**
1. `cutline doctor`. If anything fails, run `cutline deps install --all`.
2. `cutline probe` and `cutline analyze` every provided asset. Run `cutline transcribe` on spoken footage. Read the transcripts to find the story: the hook (strongest line in the first 1–3 s), the key beats, and the CTA.
3. `cutline init --target shorts`, then write `main` (story order), `layers` and `captions`. Use `auto` directives for jump cuts and fillers.
4. `cutline validate`, fix errors, then `cutline expand` to sanity-check the timeline.
5. `cutline review`, then look at `contact_sheet.jpg`, `cuts/`, `captions/` and `audio.png`, and read `summary.md`. Iterate until there are no QA errors and the suggestions are addressed.
6. `cutline render`, check `qa.json`, then report the output paths to the user, plus the publishing checklist (§12.3).

**Shorts style defaults:**
- Hook text in the first second; captions `bold_pop`; a visual change at least every 3–5 s (cut, punch-in, B-roll, graphic).
- Music ducked under the voice; SFX on transitions sparingly; progress bar on; end with a loopable last line or a CTA.

**Long-form defaults:** `clean_sentence` captions (or none), lower thirds for names, chapters, B-roll every 20–40 s, and end screen space in the last 20 s.

---

## 12. Licensing review (internal use, published output)

> This is an engineering assessment, not legal advice. Confirm anything material with counsel. The key facts: the software is used internally and not distributed or sold, and the **videos** are published.

### 12.1 Tools and components

| Component | License | OK for this use? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| FFmpeg (static builds incl. x264/x265/vidstab) | GPL-2.0+ (LGPL core) | **Yes** | GPL obligations apply on *distribution* of the binary. Internal use and running it as a separate process are fine. Output videos are not covered by the ffmpeg license. If `cutline` plus ffmpeg is later shared outside the organization, provide the ffmpeg source/offer (or switch to LGPL builds without x264). |
| H.264/AAC patents | Via LA (formerly MPEG LA) pools | Very likely yes | The AVC license historically charges no royalty for internet video that's free to end users. YouTube-hosted free content fits that. Confirm with counsel if content is sold or paywalled. |
| whisper.cpp / whisper-rs | MIT / Unlicense | Yes | |
| Whisper model weights | MIT (OpenAI) | Yes | |
| ONNX Runtime / `ort` | MIT / MIT-Apache | Yes | |
| YuNet model (OpenCV Zoo) | MIT (verify at download; record in lockfile) | Yes | |
| Chromium / Chrome for Testing | BSD-style + various | Yes | Internal tooling use |
| lottie-web | MIT | Yes | |
| chromiumoxide, clap, serde, etc. | MIT/Apache | Yes | Enforced by `cargo-deny` |
| Fonts: Inter, Montserrat, Anton, Bebas Neue, Poppins | SIL OFL 1.1 | Yes | OFL permits embedding in videos and bundling. Keep the license files in `assets/fonts/`. |
| Noto Emoji | OFL 1.1 / Apache-2.0 | Yes | Avoid Twemoji (CC-BY needs attribution) and Apple emoji (not licensed). |
| RNNoise models (`arnndn`) | Varies by model | Check per model | Not used by default; `afftdn` needs no model. |
| LUTs | Generate our own, or use CC0 sources only | Yes | Record sources in `assets/luts/SOURCES.md`. |

### 12.2 Content inputs (the real licensing risk)
- **ElevenLabs** (VO, music, SFX): commercial and publishing rights depend on the **subscription plan**. Free tiers have historically required attribution and restricted commercial use; paid plans grant commercial rights. **Action: confirm the account plan covers monetized YouTube publishing.** Voice clones need the consent of the voice owner.
- **Claude Motion / other generators:** check that tool's terms for rights to the outputs.
- **User footage, music and SFX** must be owned or licensed. The tool can't verify this. `render` writes a `credits.txt` listing all assets used, to help with attribution and audits.

### 12.3 Publishing checklist (printed after render)
- YouTube **altered/synthetic content disclosure**: when realistic AI-generated or AI-altered people, voices or scenes are present, tick the disclosure in YouTube Studio (an AI voice narrating real footage may qualify).
- Music and SFX rights confirmed (ElevenLabs plan / licenses).
- Chapters pasted into the description (long form).
- Thumbnail exported; captions also exported as `.srt` for upload (better accessibility and search). `render` always writes `<name>.srt` alongside the video.

---

## 13. Non-functional requirements
- **Performance:** a 60 s Shorts final render with captions, reframe and music on an Apple Silicon Mac takes ≤ 90 s cold and ≤ 20 s warm (after a caption-only change). Benchmarks are recorded by selftest.
- **Robustness:** handles VFR phone footage, rotated iPhone video, 10-bit HEVC, ProRes, mixed frame rates, odd sample rates and mono audio.
- **Determinism:** the same project and tools produce identical filter scripts and identical frames (bit-exact for mezzanines; within QA tolerance for the final x264 encode).
- **Observability:** `--verbose` logs every ffmpeg command. `render_report.json` includes timings per stage, cache hits, tool versions and the QA summary.
- **Disk hygiene:** temp files live in the project's `.cutline/tmp` and are cleaned on success. `cache clean --older-than 30d`.

## 14. Assumptions & open items (don't block on these)
- Claude Motion's exact output format is unknown. It's handled by accepting any ffmpeg-decodable video, alpha formats, image sequences and HTML/Lottie/SVG.
- No ElevenLabs API usage. If Scribe JSON field names differ from the fixture, the importer must be tolerant and well-tested. Update the fixture once a real file is available.
- GitHub (or similar) is available for CI. If not, the same checks run locally via `cargo xtask ci`.
- Sources for the face test fixture must be CC0/public domain. If none is obtained, reframe uses the mock-detector tests plus manual verification on user footage (logged in `PROGRESS.md`).
